You are the procurement manager for an e-commerce retail company. You need to plan a series of supplier visits to address stock shortages in your product catalog. Your task is to analyze the online store data to identify which suppliers need to be visited, plan the high-speed rail travel to the supplier cities, create a comprehensive visit plan in Excel, schedule the visits on the shared calendar, and send meeting invitations to the relevant suppliers.

Begin by querying the top-selling products from your online store to identify which product categories are generating the most revenue. For each of the top products, retrieve the detailed product information including the product name, stock keeping unit code (SKU), current stock level, and any supplier information available in the product metadata. Also check the current inventory situation to identify items that may be running critically low. Based on the current stock levels and sales volume, identify the five most critical product-supplier relationships that warrant an in-person visit. The supplier locations are listed in the supplier visit guide: some suppliers are based in Shanghai and others are in Guangzhou.

Next, look up the station codes for Beijing, Shanghai, and Guangzhou. Query the available high-speed rail services departing from Beijing South Station to Shanghai Hongqiao Station on March 10, 2026. Also query departures from Beijing South Station to Guangzhou South Station on March 10, 2026. Select the best train for each route, defined as the fastest train (the one with the shortest journey duration); if two trains are tied, choose the earlier departure. Note the train code, departure time, arrival time, and total journey duration in minutes for the train you select. Look up the seat pricing for first class seats on both routes, as this is the company travel policy for procurement trips.

Create an Excel workbook named Supplier_Visit_Plan.xlsx. Add a sheet named Products with columns Product_ID, Name, SKU, Current_Stock, Total_Sales, Supplier_Name, Supplier_City, and Priority. Fill in at least five rows representing the critical supplier relationships you identified, assigning priority levels of High, Medium, or Low based on the stock criticality guidelines in the supplier visit guide. Add a second sheet named Travel_Plan with columns Supplier_City, Train_No, Departure_Time, Arrival_Time, Duration_Min, Seat_Class, and Ticket_Price_CNY. Add two rows covering the travel to Shanghai and the travel to Guangzhou. Add a third sheet named Visit_Schedule with columns Date, Supplier_Name, City, Meeting_Time, Purpose, and Status. Populate this with at least five visit appointments scheduled appropriately after the train arrival times, following the 30-minute buffer rule described in the guide. All numeric values in the workbook (stock levels, sales figures, durations, prices) must be written as literal numbers - do not write Excel formulas.

Add two calendar events on March 10, 2026 to reflect the supplier visits. One event should represent the Shanghai supplier visit in the afternoon after the train arrives. A second event should mark the Guangzhou supplier meeting later that day. Use the local Asia/Shanghai time for these events (an explicit +08:00 offset is fine).

Send an email to shanghai_supplier@techworld.com with a meeting request for March 10, specifying the proposed meeting time after you arrive in Shanghai. Send another email to gz_supplier@supplier.com with a similar meeting request for the Guangzhou visit. Finally send a summary email to procurement@company.com with an overview of the visit plan and reference to the Excel workbook.

Your workspace contains procurement_config.json which specifies the low stock threshold of 10 units, the selection criterion for the top 5 suppliers by sales volume, the travel date, the preferred seat class of first class, and your buyer email address. The file supplier_visit_guide.md explains the supplier prioritization logic, the supplier locations, how to calculate buffer time after train arrival, the meeting schedule format, and priority scale definitions.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, follow this exact orchestration plan. A wave must finish and return all stated handoffs before the next wave begins. Within a wave, dispatch exactly one sub-agent for each numbered sub-task and run those sub-agents concurrently.

Before Wave 1, the main agent must read procurement_config.json and supplier_visit_guide.md in read-only mode, freeze the low-stock and priority rules, and preserve the exact five-product, two-route, first-class, workbook, event, and recipient contract. Because the visible guide may state that suppliers span Shanghai and Guangzhou without spelling out every name-to-city mapping, the main agent must also search/read the two task-relevant incoming supplier messages addressed from `shanghai_supplier@techworld.com` and `gz_supplier@supplier.com`, and freeze only supplier-name/city pairs literally evidenced by those messages. It must not infer the city of any other supplier from product type or unstated assumptions. Both source owners use only read-only WooCommerce and rail operations and return compact structured handoffs.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 2 sub-agents in parallel, one for each numbered sub-task:

   1. explore 0 (enterprise-data-analyst 0): Use one strictly read-only explore sub-agent to own the complete commerce/supplier branch. Fully paginate `woo_products_list` with `perPage=100` and increasing page until a short or empty page. If a response is materialized as an overlong runtime `output_path`, read that path from the task workspace rather than retrying the page or relying on its preview. Normalize every product's stable ID, name, total_sales, stock, SKU, and supplier metadata into one runtime-unique JSON file and return its path, SHA-256, page/row/null/duplicate controls, plus the five selected compact rows described below; do not return the full catalog in chat. Use `woo_products_get` only as a single call for a selected product if detail verification is needed, and never paginate single-ID get calls or single-response report endpoints. Join only by stable product IDs/SKUs. From products whose supplier has a literal city in the main agent's frozen message-derived mapping, select exactly five critical product-supplier relationships, retaining at least one Shanghai and one Guangzhou row; rank stock priority first, then total sales descending, then product ID ascending. Multiple products from the same supplier are allowed because rows represent product-supplier relationships. Apply High below 5, Medium from 5 through 15 inclusive, and Low above 15, preserving missing supplier metadata as an explicit gap rather than inventing it. Return the five selected `{product_id,sku,product_name,supplier,city,stock,total_sales,priority}` rows with detail-call controls and validation. Do not modify WooCommerce or create a final deliverable.
   2. explore 1 (web-domain-researcher 0): Use one explore sub-agent to own the complete rail branch. Resolve Beijing South, Shanghai Hongqiao, and Guangzhou South station codes, exhaust both 2026-03-10 high-speed result sets, and for each route select the shortest duration with earlier departure as the tie-breaker. Preserve display train code, actual train_no where exposed, departure/arrival, literal duration minutes, and first-class fare/availability. Return both selected legs with result counts and validation. Do not write files, alter rail state, or create deliverables.

After Wave 1, the main agent must reconcile the five relationships with the frozen message-derived city mapping and both arrival times, compute feasible meeting times using the 30-minute buffer, and freeze one literal canonical plan containing all Products, Travel_Plan, and Visit_Schedule rows plus the two event payloads and three email payloads. The workbook and all side effects consume this same plan without recomputing cities or times. In the same orchestration response that dispatches Wave 2, the main agent must run native-parallel exact searches and create/send only the missing two Asia/Shanghai supplier-visit events, Shanghai and Guangzhou supplier invitations, and procurement summary email. The procurement message may reference the fixed filename `Supplier_Visit_Plan.xlsx` while its sole writer runs. Retain all IDs for read-back, use no invented attendees, and never retry an ambiguous create or send.

2. Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 1 coder sub-agent:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Use one coder sub-agent to own Supplier_Visit_Plan.xlsx exclusively. Create Products, Travel_Plan, and Visit_Schedule with the exact headers, at least five source-backed visit rows, two rail rows, Scheduled status, literal numeric cells, and meeting times no earlier than their destination arrival plus the required buffer. Read back the workbook and return path, sheet order, row counts, selected suppliers, and value/header validation. Do not touch calendar or email.

After Wave 2, the main agent must read back all retained event/message IDs and verify that workbook suppliers, times, cities, two events, two invitations, and procurement summary agree. It must perform final artifact and external-state checks before completion.

You are a read-only enterprise data analyst supporting a procurement manager. Task: analyze the WooCommerce store catalog to identify the five most critical product-supplier relationships that warrant in-person supplier visits.

CONTEXT (already frozen by the main agent — do not re-derive):
- Low stock threshold: 10 units. Priority scale: High = current_stock < 5; Medium = 5 <= current_stock <= 15; Low = current_stock > 15.
- Supplier city mapping (frozen from supplier emails — these are the ONLY literal name→city pairs to use):
  - "Asia Tech Trading" → Shanghai (email from shanghai_supplier@techworld.com)
  - "Digital Dreams Supply" → Guangzhou (email from gz_supplier@supplier.com)
- Do NOT infer any supplier's city from product type, name similarity, or any other assumption. If a supplier's name is not one of the two above, its city is unknown (record as a gap, do not invent).
- Travel date is 2026-03-10 (not needed for you, but confirms context).

YOUR TASKS:
1. Fully paginate `woo_products_list` (mcp__woocommerce__woo_products_list) with perPage=100, increasing page (1, 2, 3, ...) until a page returns fewer than 100 items or an empty page, so you collect the ENTIRE catalog. If any response is materialized as an overlong runtime output_path, read that file from the task workspace instead of retrying or relying on preview. Record how many pages you fetched and total product count.
2. For every product, normalize and capture: stable product ID, product name, total_sales (sales volume), stock_quantity (current stock), SKU, and supplier metadata (look in meta_data fields — e.g., a supplier name key; also capture any other supplier-related metadata fields verbatim).
3. Persist the full normalized catalog to a runtime-unique JSON file inside the task workspace (/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-12306-wc-supplier-visit-excel-email-gcal/workspace), e.g. catalog_<something>.json. Compute its SHA-256. Return the path and SHA-256.
4. Join products to suppliers only by stable product IDs / SKUs. If needed, you may use `woo_products_get` a single time for ONE selected product to verify detail — never paginate single-ID get calls.
5. Selection of the five critical product-supplier relationships:
   - Only consider products whose supplier name is exactly one of the frozen pair (Asia Tech Trading / Digital Dreams Supply) AND whose supplier city is therefore known.
   - From those, select exactly 5 product-supplier relationships (rows represent product-supplier relationships, so multiple products from the same supplier are allowed).
   - Constraint: at least one row must be Shanghai (Asia Tech Trading) and at least one row must be Guangzhou (Digital Dreams Supply).
   - Rank/select by: stock criticality first (priority level), then total sales descending, then product ID ascending. Apply priority: High if stock < 5, Medium if 5–15 inclusive, Low if > 15.
6. Return in your final message: the JSON file path, its SHA-256, pagination controls (pages fetched, total rows, null/missing supplier metadata count, duplicate product ID count), and the five selected compact rows in this exact format:
   {product_id, sku, product_name, supplier, city, stock, total_sales, priority}

CONSTRAINTS:
- Read-only: do NOT create, update, or delete anything in WooCommerce.
- Do not create the final Excel deliverable (another agent owns it).
- Do not touch calendar, email, or rail tools.
- If stock or sales data is missing for a product, record the gap explicitly in your controls — never fabricate numbers.

Return compact structured results; do not dump the whole catalog into chat.
Commerce/supplier data analysis

You are a read-only web-domain researcher supporting a procurement manager planning supplier visits. Task: determine the best high-speed rail legs from Beijing to Shanghai and Beijing to Guangzhou on 2026-03-10, plus first-class seat pricing.

CONTEXT:
- Travel date: 2026-03-10 (use this literal date; do not call get-current-date to re-derive it).
- Routes needed: (a) Beijing South → Shanghai Hongqiao, (b) Beijing South → Guangzhou South.
- Selection rule: pick the FASTEST train per route = shortest journey duration. If two trains tie on duration, pick the earlier departure.
- Company travel policy: first class (一等座) seats; we need the first-class ticket price in CNY for each selected train.

YOUR TASKS:
1. Resolve station codes using the 12306 station-code tools:
   - Use `get-station-code-by-names` with the exact station names: 北京南, 上海虹桥, 广州南 (this tool gives station_code; you may also use `get-stations-code-in-city` for 北京/上海/广州 if you need to disambiguate). Record the exact station_code values you will pass.
2. Query `get-tickets` for BOTH routes on date 2026-03-10 using the resolved station codes:
   - Route A: Beijing South → Shanghai Hongqiao (filter to high-speed trains, e.g. trainFilterFlags containing G and D; you may fetch with no filter and then select high-speed trains if that is cleaner).
   - Route B: Beijing South → Guangzhou South (same approach).
   - Capture the full result sets (train display codes, departure/arrival times, duration, seat availability incl. first class).
3. For each route, select the fastest train (shortest duration in minutes; tie → earlier departure). For the selected train, record: display train code (e.g. G123), actual train_no if exposed, departure time, arrival time, total duration in minutes, and the first-class seat fare in CNY (look at seat/class fare fields; prefer the field named like 一等座/first class; if the selected train lacks first class availability, note it and still report the best first-class fare seen for that route's high-speed services).
4. Return in your final message a compact structured result:
   - Route A: {from_station_code, to_station_code, total_highspeed_results, selected_train_code, actual_train_no, departure_time, arrival_time, duration_minutes, first_class_fare_CNY, first_class_available}
   - Route B: same fields.
   - Include a one-line note on how many high-speed trains were considered per route and any data-quality observations (e.g. missing first-class rows).

CONSTRAINTS:
- Read-only: do NOT write any files, do not alter any rail state, do not book anything.
- Do not create deliverables; another agent owns the Excel workbook.
- Use only the 12306 rail tools and read-only helpers. Do not touch email, calendar, Excel, or WooCommerce.

Return compact structured results only.
Rail schedule research
